# INFECTIONS INVOLVING CARDIOVASCULAR DEVICES (EXCLUDING VALVES)

Most infections are associated with Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci.

Many of these staphylococci are resistant to methicillin, so initial empiric therapy with vancomycin is required.

Consultation with Infectious Diseases is encouraged for patients with severe allergies to vancomycin or for those who have vancomycin-resistant infections.

At least 3 blood cultures should be drawn prior to the initiation of empirical antimicrobial. Modify antimicrobial regimen and narrow coverage based on results of culture and susceptibility tests Infectious Disease and Cardiothoracic surgery consultations are encouraged.

Device removal is necessary for cure in most cases. However, it may be difficult depending on the nature of the device and specific clinical circumstances. Device removal should be discussed with Cardiology, Infectious Disease, or Cardiothoracic surgery consultants.

If the device removal is not possible, add rifampin.

# Duration of therapy

Duration of therapy should be determined in concert with Cardiology, Infectious Disease, or Cardiothoracic surgery consultants.

Therapy:
## Empiric treatment in cases where device removal is planned

Vancomycin IV Pharmacy to dose

## Empiric treatment in cases where surgery cannot be performed

Vancomycin IV Pharmacy to dose <AND> rifampin 300 mg PO/NG q8h ($)

[DI,O]

## For hemodynamically unstable patients, add gentamicin to one of the above treatment regimens

< ADD > gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h ($) R,O
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU ABX INFECT INVOLVES CARD DEVICES
